<DIV style="width: 87%; margin-left: 6%"><!-- BEGIN LOGICAL PAGE -->

<DIV style="margin-top: 18pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">K&#38;F
    INDUSTRIES HOLDINGS, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <B>NOTES&#160;TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL
    STATEMENTS&#160;&#151;&#160;(Continued)</B>
</DIV>
<P>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    (b)&#160;the eurodollar rate, which will be the rate at which
    eurodollar deposits for one, two, three or six or (if available
    to all lenders under the relevant facility, as determined by
    such lenders in their sole discretion) nine or twelve months are
    offered in the interbank eurodollar market. The applicable
    margin for the revolving credit facility is currently 1.50% with
    respect to the base rate loans and 2.50% with respect to
    eurodollar loans. The applicable margin for the term loan
    facility is currently 1.25% with respect to base rate loans and
    2.25% with respect to eurodollar loans. Upon the occurrence of
    any payment default, all outstanding amounts under the Credit
    Facility will bear interest at a rate equal to the rate then in
    effect with respect to such borrowings, plus 2%&#160;per annum.
    K&#38;F Industries is also obligated to pay a commission on all
    outstanding letters of credit in the amount of an applicable
    margin then in effect with respect to eurodollar loans under the
    revolving credit facility as well as fronting fees on the
    aggregate drawable amount of all outstanding letters of credit.
    The weighted average interest rate on outstanding indebtedness
    under the Credit Facility was 6.6% at December&#160;31, 2005.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Credit Facility contains customary representations and
    warranties, covenants and conditions to borrowing.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Credit Facility contains a number of negative covenants that
    limit K&#38;F Industries and its subsidiaries from, among other
    things, incurring other indebtedness, entering into merger or
    consolidation transactions, disposing of all or substantially
    all of their assets, making certain restricted payments, paying
    dividends, making capital expenditures, creating any liens on
    its subsidiaries&#146; assets, creating guarantee obligations
    and material lease obligations and entering into sale and
    leaseback transactions and transactions with affiliates.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Credit Facility also requires the maintenance of certain
    quarterly financial and operating ratios, including a
    consolidated cash interest coverage ratio and consolidated
    leverage ratio. At December&#160;31, 2005, K&#38;F Industries
    was in compliance with all covenants. At December&#160;31, 2005,
    K&#38;F Industries&#146; actual consolidated cash interest ratio
    was 2.40 to 1 versus 1.65 to 1, as required by the credit
    agreement, and K&#38;F Industries&#146; actual consolidated
    leverage ratio was 5.98 to 1 versus 7.75 to 1, as required by
    the credit agreement.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Credit Facility also contains customary events of default,
    including default upon the nonpayment of principal, interest,
    fees or other amounts or the occurrence of a change of control.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Credit Facility provides for revolving loans not to exceed
    $50.0&#160;million, with up to $10&#160;million available for
    letters of credit. The revolving loan commitment terminates on
    November&#160;18, 2010. At December&#160;31, 2005, K&#38;F had
    $48.3&#160;million available to borrow under the revolving
    credit facility and $1.7&#160;million of letters of credit
    outstanding.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

    2005 and 2004, respectively. The estimated fair value of the
    Company&#146;s outstanding indebtedness on the Credit Facility
    approximates its fair value because the interest rates on the
    debt are reset on a frequent basis to reflect current market
    rates.

<DIV style="margin-top: 3pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As a requirement of our Credit Facility, K&#38;F entered into
    the following: (i)&#160;a 3&#160;month LIBOR interest rate cap
    at 6% from December 2005 to December 2007 for an increasing
    notional amount starting at $144.6&#160;million, increasing to
    $161.2&#160;million; (ii)&#160;a swap arrangement for a portion
    of our term loans from a variable 3&#160;month LIBOR interest
    rate to a fixed rate of 4.0375%, beginning January 24, 2006. The
    notional amount of the swaps is initially $95.4&#160;million and
    declines to $78.8&#160;million on January&#160;24, 2008 at the
    termination of the swap agreement; and (iii)&#160;a swap
    arrangement for a portion of our term loans from a variable
    3&#160;month LIBOR interest rate to a fixed rate of 4.506%,
    beginning January&#160;24, 2006. The notional amount of the
    swaps is initially $47.7&#160;million and declines to
    $39.4&#160;million on January 24, 2008 at the termination of the
    swap agreement.

    13,300,000&#160;shares, respectively.

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <I>Junior Redeemable Exchangeable Preferred
    Stock</I>&#160;&#151;&#160;Authorized Junior Redeemable
    Exchangeable Preferred Stock (the &#147;Junior Preferred
    Stock&#148;) of K&#38;F consists of 20,000&#160;shares, par
    value $.01&#160;per share. The total number of shares of Junior
    Preferred Stock of K&#38;F issued and outstanding at
    December&#160;31, 2005 and 2004 was 0&#160;shares and
    12,250&#160;shares, respectively. The Junior Preferred Stock
    ranks senior to K&#38;F&#146;s common stock as to dividend
    rights or upon liquidation but is non-voting except as required
    by law. Dividends accrue on the Junior Preferred Stock at a rate
    per annum equal to 10% of the liquidation preference. The Junior
    Preferred Stock is subject to redemption at any time, in whole
    or in part, at the option of K&#38;F at a redemption price to
    liquidation preference and is subject to a mandatory change of
    control redemption upon the occurrence of a change of control of
    K&#38;F at the liquidation preference. The shares of Junior
    Preferred Stock are exchangeable at the sole option of K&#38;F
    for subordinated exchange debentures of K&#38;F. In the event of
    any liquidation, dissolution or winding up of K&#38;F, the
    holders of the Junior Preferred Stock will be entitled to
    receive a liquidation preference equal to the stated value of
    $10,000 plus all accrued but unpaid dividends.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <TD width="95%"></TD>

<TR valign="top">
    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">11.&#160;&#160;</FONT></B>
</TD>
    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Employee
    Benefit Plans</FONT></B>
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company provides pension benefits to substantially all
    employees through hourly and salaried pension plans. The plans
    provide benefits based primarily on the participant&#146;s years
    of service, and for the salary plan level of compensation as
    well. The salaried plan also includes voluntary employee
    contributions. The Company&#146;s funding policy is to
    contribute the minimum required under the Employee Retirement
    Income Security Act of 1974 (&#147;ERISA&#148;).
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company provides postretirement health care and life
    insurance benefits for all eligible employees and their
    dependents. Participants are eligible for these benefits when
    they retire from active service and meet the eligibility
    requirements of the Company&#146;s pension plans. The health
    care plans are generally contributory and the life insurance
    plans are generally non-contributory.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company uses a measurement date of December&#160;31 for its
    pension and postretirement plans.
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <BR>
    F-18

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The projected benefit obligation, accumulated benefit obligation
    and fair value of plan assets for the pension plans with
    accumulated benefit obligations in excess of plan assets were
    $163.1&#160;million, $155.9&#160;million and
    $104.8&#160;million, respectively, as of December&#160;31, 2005
    and $150.1&#160;million, $144.7&#160;million and
    $102.3&#160;million, respectively, as of December&#160;31, 2004.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In the fourth quarter of 2003 the Company announced to all
    active salaried and the majority of its retired salaried
    employees that effective January&#160;1, 2012 it would freeze
    its share of the retiree health care costs at the 2011 employer
    cost level. This announcement was also made to all Aircraft
    Braking Systems&#146; retired bargaining employees or their
    continuing beneficiaries.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In determining the expected long-term rate of return on assets,
    the Company evaluated input from its investment consultants,
    actuaries and investment management firm, including their review
    of asset class return expectations, as well as long-term
    historical asset class returns. Projected returns by such
    consultants and economists are based on broad equity and bond
    indices. Additionally, the Company considered its most recent
    four year compounded returns, which have been in excess of
    K&#38;F&#146;s forward-looking return expectations. The
    Company&#146;s current asset manager has invested K&#38;F&#146;s
    pension assets over the last four years.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company&#146;s pension plan weighted-average asset
    allocations by asset category, were as follows:
</DIV>

    The Company&#146;s investment policy is to maximize the total
    rate of return (income and appreciation) with a view to the
    long-term funding objectives of the pension plans. Therefore,
    the pension plan assets are diversified to the extent necessary
    to minimize risks and to achieve an optimal balance between risk
    and return and between income

<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always">&nbsp;</H5><P>

<DIV style="width: 87%; margin-left: 6%"><!-- BEGIN LOGICAL PAGE -->

<DIV style="margin-top: 18pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">K&#38;F
    INDUSTRIES HOLDINGS, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <B>NOTES&#160;TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL
    STATEMENTS&#160;&#151;&#160;(Continued)</B>
</DIV>
<P>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    and growth of assets through capital appreciation. The
    Company&#146;s policy is to allocate pension plan funds within a
    target for each major asset category.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In December 2003, the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement
    and Modernization Act of 2003 was enacted. The Act introduced a
    plan sponsor subsidy based on a percentage of a
    beneficiary&#146;s annual prescription drug benefits, within
    defined limits, and the opportunity for a retiree to obtain
    prescription drug benefits under Medicare.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In May 2004, the FASB issued FSP
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">No.&#160;106-2,</FONT>
    &#147;Accounting and Disclosure Requirements Related to the
    Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement and Modernization
    Act,&#148; which supersedes FSP
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">No.&#160;106-1</FONT>
    of the same title. The Staff Position clarifies the accounting
    for the benefits attributable to new government subsidies for
    companies that provide prescription drug benefits to retirees.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As of December&#160;31, 2003, the Company had elected to defer
    any accounting for the effects of the Act pursuant to FSP
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">No.&#160;106-1.</FONT>
    The Company adopted FSP
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">No.&#160;106-2</FONT>
    as of July&#160;1, 2004, the beginning of our third quarter,
    retroactive to January&#160;1, 2004. The Company determined that
    benefits provided by the plan were at least actuarially
    equivalent to Medicare Part&#160;D. The Company remeasured the
    effects of the Act on the recorded APBO as of January&#160;1,
    2004. The effect of the federal subsidy to which we are entitled
    has been estimated to decrease the APBO by approximately
    $10.5&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The decrease in the APBO was treated as a gain, which was
    amortized from January&#160;1, 2004. The table below details the
    reduction in net periodic postretirement cost by component,
    which is included in the results of operations for the periods
    presented below, as a result of the Act and the adoption of FSP
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">No.&#160;106-2.</FONT>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During 2005, the Company finalized the allocation of purchase
    price relating to the Acquisition. This resulted in the
    reallocation of approximately $126&#160;million from customer
    relationships to Program Participation Costs. The estimated
    average useful life is 25&#160;years for both of these
    intangible assets. Amortization of Program Participation Costs
    is recorded as a charge to cost of sales while amortization of
    customer relationships is charged to amortization of intangible
    assets. This adjustment will have no effect on net income,
    however, gross profit will be reduced by approximately
    $5&#160;million per year, for the life of this asset, and
    amortization of intangibles will be reduced by the same amount.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Undistributed earnings of the Company&#146;s foreign
    subsidiaries amounted to approximately $5.7 million. Those
    earnings are considered to be permanently reinvested, and
    accordingly, no U.S. federal and state income taxes have been
    provided thereon. Upon distribution in the form of dividends or
    otherwise, the Company would be subject to U.S. income taxes
    (subject to foreign tax credits) and withholding taxes payable
    to the various foreign countries. Determination of the amount of
    unrecognized deferred U.S. income tax liability is not practical
    because of the complexities associated with its hypothetical
    calculation;  however, such taxes may be reduced by tax credits
    and other deductions.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company had approximately $3.8&#160;million of alternative
    minimum tax credits which do not expire.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company had approximately $3.1&#160;million of general
    business credit carryforwards, of which $0.4&#160;million will
    expire in calendar year 2006;  another $0.5&#160;million will
    expire between 2012 and 2015; and $2.2&#160;million will expire
    between 2016 and 2019.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company had U.S. federal net operating losses in the amount
    of approximately $9.4 million which will begin to expire in
    calendar year 2024. The Company had state net operating losses
    of approximately $33.6 million which will begin to expire in
    2010.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company had approximately $0.3&#160;million of foreign tax
    credits, of which $0.1&#160;million will expire in calendar year
    2011 and the balance will expire in 2012 and 2013.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company had approximately $0.3&#160;million of Ohio tax
    credits which will begin to expire by $0.1&#160;million per year
    beginning in calendar year 2006.

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company&#146;s activities are conducted through its two
    wholly owned subsidiaries, Aircraft Braking Systems and
    Engineered Fabrics, each considered an operating segment.
    Aircraft Braking Systems manufactures aircraft wheels, brakes
    and brake control systems. Engineered Fabrics manufactures
    aircraft fuel tanks and iceguards and various other products
    from coated fabrics. The accounting policies of the subsidiaries
    are the same as those described in the summary of significant
    accounting policies. Both subsidiaries are managed separately
    due to different products, technology and marketing strategies.
    The Company evaluates performance of the subsidiaries based on
    profits from operations before interest, income taxes and
    extraordinary charges (&#147;Operating Profits&#148;).
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    K&#38;F has no independent assets or operations. Obligations
    under the
    7<FONT style="vertical-align: top; font-size: 70&#37;">3</FONT>/<FONT style="font-size: 70&#37;">4</FONT>%&#160;Notes
    are fully and unconditionally guaranteed by all of
    K&#38;F&#146;s domestic subsidiaries, on a joint and several
    basis. As almost all of the Company&#146;s revenues and profits
    are derived from the subsidiaries which guarantee the
    7<FONT style="vertical-align: top; font-size: 70&#37;">3</FONT>/<FONT style="font-size: 70&#37;">4</FONT>%&#160;Notes,
    the other subsidiaries of K&#38;F, which are foreign
    subsidiaries, are not material to the Company.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

    Company&#146;s segments:
